stem: Tejas writes $120 = 2^{3} \times 3 \times 5$. He asks whether $24$ is a factor of $120$.

options.text: Yes, because $24 = 2^{3} \times 3$ uses only prime factors that appear in $120$.
No, because a factor must use every prime factor of $120$, including $5$.
Yes, because $120$ is a factor of $24$.
The check is settled by finding the HCF of every pair of whole numbers near $120$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: 24 = 2³ × 3 is built from primes available in 120 = 2³ × 3 × 5, and 24 × 5 = 120.

teacher.key_rationale: 24 = 2³×3 is a subproduct of 120's primes, so 24 divides 120. B wrongly requires every prime. C reverses factor and multiple. D switches to an HCF hunt.
